To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
small rivers are crucial components of the terrestrial river networks in the Arctic, and they have a significant influence on streamflow travel time and carbon cycle.
small rivers are crucial components of river networks in the Colville River basin in Alaska.

(1), small rivers occupy > 80% of total length and surface area, and drain > 90% of the Col- ville River Basin catchment area; and (2), including numerous small rivers shortens mean hillslope- channel travel time by an order of magnitude, and increases peak of hillslope- channel traveltime distribution by 4 times.

the hydrography of Arctic rivers and the impact of small Arctic rivers.
the role that small Arctic rivers play in hydrological and biogeochemical processes.
the role of small rivers in the hydrography of Arctic river networks and the implications of this role for carbon dioxide emissions.

the inclusion of small rivers in the Colville River network increases the peak of the hillslope-channel travel-time distribution by ∼4×, shortens the mean travel time by at last an order of magnitude, and accounts for 87% of CO2 emissions from the Colville River basin.

the inclusion of numerous small rivers in the river hydrograph increases the peak of the hillslope-channel travel-time distribution (TTD), and decreases the mean hillslope channel travel-time, by an order of magnitude, relative to the coarser resolution river hydrography product.

small rivers are important components of the Arctic river network, but have been largely overlooked due to their spatial scale.
